rationale: C01 supplies the specific decision-making machinery expressly reflected in the child: Tariff Commission escape-clause reports are reviewed with advice from the Trade Policy Committee before the President decides what action to take. This is more concrete than a shared trade-policy topic and plausibly structures the child's opening account of receiving the reports, obtaining committee advice, and making commodity-specific decisions. C14 parallels the distinction between Commission findings and independent presidential judgment, while C09 provides a model for accepting an injury finding and increasing a duty, but neither matches the child's administrative sequence as closely as C01.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Tariff Commission has furnished me with reports and supplemental information regarding escape clause investigations... I have carefully considered these reports and obtained the advice of the Trade Policy Committee.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Trade Policy Committee shall make recommendations to the President as to what action, if any, he should take on reports submitted to him by the United States Tariff Commission pursuant to section 7 of the Trade Agreements Extension Act of 1951
shared_material.explanation: The child directly instantiates C01's prescribed sequence: Tariff Commission report, Trade Policy Committee advice, and presidential consideration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I concur in the findings of injury made by the Committee... and I have issued proclamations promulgating increases in duties upon these commodities.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Trade Policy Committee shall make recommendations to the President as to what action, if any, he should take
shared_material.explanation: The child's acceptance of some injury findings and resulting tariff action is the substantive presidential decision contemplated by C01.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is my judgment that the increases in duties recommended for ceramic mosaic tile and baseball and softball gloves and mitts should not be placed in effect.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: what action, if any, he should take on reports submitted to him by the United States Tariff Commission
shared_material.explanation: The phrase 'if any' accommodates the same report-by-report choice reflected in the child's rejection of recommended relief for two products.
